note.summary: We can't tell how this image was made. No signed record and no concern was found, and that is not evidence either way.

evidence.finding: Community Forensics detector score 0.001 out of 1. This score raises no concern on its own.
evidence.proves: Only that this detector did not raise a concern, and its threshold has not passed its test.
evidence.does_not_prove: A low score is not proof that a camera took it. Many AI images score low, especially after compression or from generators the model never saw.

gate.reason: original: false-positive upper bound 9.718% is above 2%

evidence.finding: Second Look's own watermark was not found: 139 of 256 bits match our message, near the 128 expected by chance.
evidence.proves: Only that our own mark is not readable in this copy.
evidence.does_not_prove: The absence of a mark says nothing about how the image was made. This looks only for Second Look's own mark. It does not detect Meta AI images or any other company's watermark.

raw.model: Meta Video Seal 1.0 (image model y_256b_img, TorchScript)

evidence.finding: Checked: c2pa, iptc, exif, classifier, watermark. None found a signed provenance record, an AI label in the metadata, or a classifier score that raises a concern.
evidence.proves: Only that the checks listed here found nothing on this file.
evidence.does_not_prove: Not finding anything does not show how the image was made: metadata is easily stripped, and the classifier is not reliable on every image. It is not evidence either way.

evidence.finding: politifact.com reviewed the claim “Photo shows the U.S. Pentagon “is under attack.”” and rated it “Pants on Fire” (publication date not given in the feed): https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2023/may/25/facebook-posts/fake-photo-used-in-claim-that-the-pentagon-was-att/ The feed lists the author as “PolitiFact”. Search words came from a model reading of your caption; check them.
evidence.proves: That politifact.com, a fact-checker on the IFCN list, published this rating on a claim that shares 4 of the 4 key words in the picked words and is 4 key words long itself. It is not necessarily the claim you are checking.
evidence.does_not_prove: That the words searched for are the claim they reviewed, or that the rating still holds. Second Look gives no true or false verdict of its own.
